items.title: Dave Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: in the days of Buddy Bolden and so forth it was

ctx.x: But then you could, you know, that’d be cool you could have a battle of the bands and put them on the wagon and tie the wagon together. The kids would love that, are you kidding? They just would, I think they’d eat that up. And I just looked a little bit inside but I saw some scores, you have scores for music that — let me see if I’m stating this correctly — traditional jazz for the most part was, when the fellows originally did it, was improvised sort of on the spot, or am I incorrect?

Well I mean I suppose it began largely in the brass bands as brass band players began to improvise. By the time it was recorded it was a more structured thing, that’s that classic New Orleans sound that I was talking about. But probably in the earliest days, in the days of Buddy Bolden and so forth it was — actually those bands played a lot of sort of arrangements I guess.
